items.note: Fetched (HTTP 200). Page title matches; page is dated 16.3.2026. Says City Board approved principles and zone boundaries for paid parking, decided to end EV discount; expansion to five city centres and metro/rail station surroundings; zone 1 EUR 3.5/h, zone 2 EUR 2.5/h; Mon-Fri 8-20, Sat 8-18, zone 1 also Sun 8-18; sports areas stay free; review of revenues/costs incl. split with parking-app firms to Board in spring 2027. The page itself gives no meeting date (item 1/2 pages say 2 March 2026; items 4/5 cite Board minutes of 16 March 2026 item 82). The Council (not Board) set the starting points in the 2026 budget. Overlaps with items 1 and 2.

Fetched; title 'Expansion of paid parking', published 24.3.2026. Page says the City Board approved the principles on 2 March 2026 (this page's date; minutes cited elsewhere are 16 March). Two errors in the draft: (a) the EUR 2.5m (2026) / EUR 4.5m (later years) revenue estimate is attributed on the page to the PRICE INCREASE, not to the expansion plus end of the EV discount; (b) the page does not say park-and-ride stays free, it says park-and-ride PRICES remain unchanged. Zone 300 m / 600 m, EUR 80 fine pending Ministry approval, and gradual rollout (estimated summer and autumn 2026) are correct, the latter an estimate. Overlaps with items 0, 2, 3.
items.corrected_text: City of Espoo news (24 March 2026) says the City Board approved on 2 March 2026 the principles for expanding paid parking and new zone boundaries, and decided to end the 50% EV discount. Zone 1 covers densely populated areas within about 300 m of the city centre and zone 2 extends to about 600 m. A higher EUR 80 fine in zone 1 would apply if the Ministry of the Interior approves the proposal. The city estimates that the price increase (EUR 3.5/h zone 1, EUR 2.5/h zone 2, in force since early 2026) will bring EUR 2.5 million extra revenue in 2026 and EUR 4.5 million in following years. Paid parking is to take effect gradually as traffic signs are installed, estimated during summer and autumn 2026. Park-and-ride prices remain unchanged.

items.corrected_text: On 17 June 2026 Espoo announced that, under the City Board's March 2026 decision, it would start updating traffic signs in the Kaitaa and Leppavaara areas in June; fees take effect immediately once signs are replaced (zone 1 EUR 3.50/h, zone 2 EUR 2.50/h; Mon-Fri 8-20, Sat 8-18, zone 1 also Sun 8-18).

Fetched; title matches; dated 23.3.2026. Content as drafted (abolish parking norm in new construction, 1 space per 130 m2 or at least 0.5 per dwelling near metro stations, committee deviates downward regularly) and correctly labelled an initiative. But the page lists 26 signatory names (Kurronen Sanna ... Ilkko-Ervasti Pauliina), not 27. Page does not say 'environment and building committee approves fewer than norm' beyond 'regularly deviates downward' (fine).
items.corrected_text: A council initiative dated 23 March 2026, signed by 26 councillors, proposes abolishing mandatory parking-space norms for new construction so that parking is built as needed at market price and paid for by its users. It states that near metro stations Espoo still requires one space per 130 square metres of floor area or at least 0.5 spaces per dwelling, and that the environment and building committee already regularly deviates downward from the norm. This is an initiative (proposal), not a decision.

Minimum spaces set in the zoning plan, 'not too few, not too many', and removal of free street parking aims to move parking to housing companies' spaces are on the page. items.corrected_text: MTV Uutiset reported in September 2022 that, according to Espoo's traffic planning manager Susanna Kaitanen, the minimum number of parking spaces is set in the zoning plan and the city's task is to ensure a sufficient number, neither too few nor too many. She said removing free street parking aims to shift parking to housing companies' own spaces.

items.corrected_text: Sello's parking page states that its car parks, partly under the shopping centre and partly on the roof, have a total of 2,900 spaces, and that Selloparkki is also available to customers. Parking is free for three hours per day per car; the underground car park has 48 EV charging spaces, and there is an underground park-and-ride car park open to Sello customers after 16:00 on weekdays and all day at weekends. The page is undated.

corrected_summary: Espoo is expanding paid on-street parking to its city centres and metro and rail station surroundings: the Council set EUR 3.50/h (zone 1) and EUR 2.50/h (zone 2) from 1 January 2026, and the City Board approved the expansion principles in March 2026 (dated 2 March on the city's English news pages and 16 March in the minutes it cites). The 50% EV discount ended on 19 April 2026, and signs were announced to be replaced area by area, from June in Kaitaa and Leppavaara and from October in Tapiola and Otaniemi. Park-and-ride is priced separately, for example EUR 2 for 12 hours at Kivenlahti and at Tapiola Park with an HSL ticket, while the Raide-Jokeri light rail has run since 21 October 2023 and Espoonlahti metro station has its entrances in Lippulaiva.
